clue.text: Gritty substance tending to rub

definitions.meaning: a material such as sandpaper grit used for scouring or polishing
an adjective for something that scrapes or wears away, or a manner that grates on people

explanation.definitionFit: The same word serves as the noun for a scouring material and the adjective for anything that scrapes, so both halves name it.

clue.text: Majestic time

definitions.meaning: an adjective meaning grand, venerable, inspiring awe
a period of the year, here the eighth month

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means stately and dignified, while the capitalised noun is the summer month, a stretch of the calendar.

clue.text: Braille chart?

parts.note: Braille is read by touch through raised dots, so a chart for it would be one whose surface stands up in bumps, like a map showing hills in raised form

explanation.surface: A tactile chart printed for blind readers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartographic model showing terrain in raised three-dimensional form, which could be read by fingertips just as Braille is.

clue.text: One of a number holding up the train

definitions.text: One of a number holding up the train

parts.words: One of a number holding up the train
parts.note: suggests something delaying a railway service, but means one of the many wooden or concrete beams laid under the rails, literally supporting the train

explanation.surface: Something among many that is delaying a railway service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding up' reads as delaying; it actually means physically supporting. In Britain the cross-beams under railway track carry this name (Americans say 'ties').
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-timbers beneath railway lines bear the weight of passing rolling stock, so each literally holds the carriages up.

clue.text: Church attendant almost on edge

indicators.note: almost tells us to stop just short of the complete word, dropping its final letter

parts.note: a verger is an official who looks after a church and leads processions

explanation.surface: A church official is close to losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' looks like a phrase meaning nervous, but 'on' is just a link and 'edge' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A border or margin, like the grass strip beside a road.

clue.text: Refrain at dawn?

parts.note: refrain looks like a verb meaning hold back, but it is the repeated part of a song

explanation.surface: Holding back as the sun comes up.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrain is the repeated section of a song sung by all, and the morning birdsong is known by this name.

clue.text: Reduction in overheads?

parts.note: overheads sounds like business running costs, but read literally it means what grows on top of the head, so trimming it is a visit to the barber

explanation.surface: A company trimming its running costs.
explanation.walkthrough: Overheads are a business's fixed running costs; read literally, the word means what sits on top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A barber's trim shortens hair, the growth over one's head; the word is also financial slang for a cut in value.

clue.text: Metal pin used to drive through inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the letters sit within the run of the words drive through, ignoring the space

explanation.surface: A fastener used to push through something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used to' is a link; the letters lie inside 'dRIVE Through'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short metal bolt hammered flat at the end to fasten plates together.

clue.text: Grating trends it disrupted

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters of trends it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A harsh noise as fashions are upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh and loud in sound, like a jarring, rasping voice.

clue.text: Beside nurse, one putting in an appearance

parts.note: to be at something is to be beside it, as in at the door
to nurse is to tend, so one who nurses is a tender

explanation.surface: Someone at a nurse's side turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who turns up or is present at an event, such as a regular at church.

clue.text: Dog that shines at fetching game?

definitions.text: Dog that shines at fetching game?

parts.words: Dog that shines at fetching game?
parts.note: a gundog bred to bring back shot birds, with a gleaming yellow coat; shines suggests both excelling and a lustrous gilt colour

explanation.surface: A hound that excels at bringing back birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shines' points both to excelling and to the gilt colour of the coat; 'game' is shot birds, not a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular gundog breed with a gilt-coloured coat, trained to bring back shot birds.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical point

parts.note: sounds like a matter of church doctrine, but means the tall tapering structure topping a church tower

explanation.surface: A matter of church law.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall pointed spire rising from a church tower.

clue.text: Once quoted as having been aroused

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife, so it stands for once
to be cited is to be quoted as a source

explanation.surface: Someone formerly referenced is now stirred up.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred up or thrilled; to rouse feeling is to stimulate it.

clue.text: Better when one member wandered about

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
MP stands for Member of Parliament
roved means wandered around aimlessly

explanation.surface: Things were better once a parliamentarian went on a stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Made superior or brought up to a higher standard; an enhanced thing is the better one.

clue.text: Vehicle having arrived I will put inside compound

indicators.note: put inside means one piece is placed within the others

parts.note: a van is a goods vehicle
a train that has arrived is in
contracted to I'll

explanation.surface: A truck pulls up and I'll load something into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' is a link; 'put inside' splits the vehicle-plus-arrived pair to take the contraction. Vanillin is the chemical behind vanilla's flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical substance giving vanilla its flavour; a compound in the chemistry sense.

clue.text: Got in violent animal

indicators.note: violent suggests the letters of got in are thrown about wildly

explanation.surface: A fierce beast got inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid offspring of a male tiger and a lioness, a big-cat creature.

clue.text: Racer's not a dark horse!

parts.note: a dark horse is an unexpected winner; read literally, this racer is a pale, ashen-coloured dog rather than a horse at all

explanation.surface: A competitor whose chances everyone already knows.
explanation.walkthrough: A dark horse is an unknown contender; here the 'not dark' runner is grey, and is a hound instead of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim, fast breed of dog raced on tracks after a mechanical hare.

clue.text: Bars having no meeting-place

parts.note: suggests pubs with no room for gatherings, but describes lines or rods that run side by side forever without touching, as on the gymnastics apparatus

explanation.surface: Pubs lacking a function room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' looks like pubs; it is the gymnastic apparatus of two equidistant rails, and lines of that kind never meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines running alongside each other at a constant distance never intersect, and the gymnasts' twin-rail apparatus carries the name.

clue.text: Have jelly when picture is showing

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: Eat jelly while a film is on.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury gelatine made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Explosive utterance, not an instrument to be used in surgery

definitions.text: instrument to be used in surgery

indicators.note: explosive suggests the letters of utterance are blown apart and reassembled

parts.note: the letters of an are excluded from the mix, as the word not signals

explanation.surface: An outburst of speech that isn't a surgical tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive' scrambles UTTERANCE and 'not an' takes out A and N, leaving UTTERCE to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A small scoop-shaped surgical tool for scraping tissue from a body cavity.

clue.text: It is mainly to the east of Britain

definitions.text: It is mainly to the east of Britain

parts.words: It is mainly to the east of Britain
parts.note: mainly hints at the main, an old word for the ocean, so this is the stretch of water lying off England's eastern coast

explanation.surface: A statement of geography about what lies beyond England's east coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' seems to mean mostly, but also hints at the main, an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of water between Great Britain and Scandinavia, off the British eastern coastline.

clue.text: It is not easy to include short answer in this record

indicators.note: to include means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: hard means difficult, not easy
ans is a standard abbreviation of answer

explanation.surface: Getting a brief reply into this document is difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: Hansard is the official verbatim record of debates in the UK Parliament; 'to include' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The published transcript of parliamentary proceedings, an official written account.

clue.text: Talk at endless rate on church

indicators.note: endless says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: speed is a rate of movement

explanation.surface: A lecture about non-stop progress on the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims the rate word and 'on' is a link meaning the church abbreviation follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: An address delivered to an audience, such as a lecture or oration.

clue.text: Shock about soldiers' clothing

indicators.note: about means the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: to appal is to shock or horrify
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Outrage over the troops' uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' signals the container; the shock word takes the British spelling with one L, and the Royal Engineers are a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments or dress, a formal word for what people wear.

clue.text: Remarkable painting Ann left to live in dirty surroundings

indicators.note: remarkable splits as re-markable: the letters are marked out again in a new order

parts.note: the letters of Ann are taken away, as the word left signals

explanation.surface: A notable picture that Ann abandoned for squalor.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A, N, N from PAINTING ('Ann left') to leave PITIG, which 'Remarkable' rearranges. Pig it is British slang for living like a swine.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for dwelling in squalor, like farm animals in a sty.

clue.text: More expensive drink first leading to a fight

indicators.note: first says the drink comes at the front, before the other piece

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink served from a bowl
prices that are up have risen

explanation.surface: Pricier booze sets off a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl or fistfight, informal British slang for a scrap.

clue.text: Picture dish that's easy to make before giving thanks

parts.note: pie, from the idiom 'easy as pie'
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A simple recipe made before saying grace.
explanation.walkthrough: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of Mary holding the dead Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: An artwork depicting the Virgin Mary cradling Christ's body, a common subject in painting.

clue.text: Reading matter that is illuminating

parts.note: suggests an enlightening book, but literally a text that gives off brightness; the phrase also names easy, undemanding fiction

explanation.surface: An enlightening book.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy, entertaining fiction is so called, and taken literally the phrase means writing that gives off brightness.

clue.text: Refuse puppies

definitions.meaning: rubbish or waste dropped carelessly, a noun here
a group of young dogs born to one mother at the same time

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both rubbish strewn in public and a brood of young born together, as a dog's pups.

clue.text: Fifty-one had repeatedly become affectedly superior

indicators.note: become signals the letters turning into something new, a rearrangement

parts.note: LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word had is used twice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone of fifty-one has grown snobbish.
explanation.walkthrough: LI plus HAD twice (LIHADHAD) is rearranged, as 'become' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentiously posh or snooty in manner, like someone putting on airs.
